bug_description.normalized: The odp_target harness passes an attacker-controlled NUL-terminated action string into odp_actions_from_string(). In parse_odp_action(), the set(...) branch allocates a stack struct nlattr mask[] and wraps it in an empty ofpbuf stub. The staged witness string uses a set payload that is only a valid ufid:<uuid> token. parse_odp_key_mask_attr() accepts that UFID and returns its length immediately, but this success path appends neither a key nlattr to the action buffer nor a mask nlattr to maskbuf. parse_odp_action() then checks only that the next character is ')' and calls nl_attr_get_size(mask) as if mask[0] were a populated struct nlattr. nl_attr_get_size() reads mask[0].nla_len from uninitialized stack memory, and MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value. The staged fix removes UFID handling from parse_odp_key_mask_attr() and handles UFID only in odp_flow_from_string(), where that token is valid.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the attacker-controlled set-action payload and routes it into the generic key/mask parser together with the stack-backed mask buffer.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is the NUL-terminated ASCII string `set(ufid:cb999996-9996-0996-0447-009000000009)`. After the `set(` prefix, line 2221 passes the exact payload beginning with `ufid:cb999996-9996-0996-0447-009000000009` into parse_odp_key_mask_attr().

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant uninitialized state is the stack array `mask` that backs `maskbuf`. `maskbuf` is initialized as an empty stub at line 2216, so if no mask attribute is written then `mask[0].nla_len` stays indeterminate when later treated as a struct nlattr header.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. nl_attr_get_size() reads the `nla_len` field from the caller-supplied pointer even though no struct nlattr header was ever written to the stack-backed `mask` buffer.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `nl_attr_get_size` at `lib/netlink.c:598:5` and says the poisoned value was created by allocation of `mask` in the stack frame of `parse_odp_action`.

root_cause.description: The generic key/mask parser treats `ufid:` as a successful parse in every caller context and returns its length immediately, even though this path appends no key attribute to `actions` and no mask attribute to `maskbuf`.
root_cause.note: For a `set(...)` action the caller expects nested nlattrs after this helper returns. The UFID fast path violates that contract: it reports success but leaves the stack-backed `maskbuf` empty, so later size calculations dereference uninitialized `mask[0]`. The fix removes UFID handling from parse_odp_key_mask_attr() and moves it to odp_flow_from_string(), where UFID is actually valid.

parser_admitted.condition: The staged PoC is 47 bytes long, ends with a NUL byte, contains no newline, and has no embedded NUL before the terminator, so `strlen(input) == size - 1` and the harness admits it before calling parse_actions() on the raw action string.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness admits a single-line NUL-terminated witness string and passes it to parse_actions(), which calls odp_actions_from_string() on attacker-controlled OVS action text.

The set-action parser allocates a stack-backed mask buffer, parses the payload `ufid:...` through parse_odp_key_mask_attr(), and the UFID fast path returns success without materializing any key or mask nlattr.

parse_odp_action() only verifies that the UFID is followed by `)` and then calls nl_attr_get_size(mask) as if `mask` held a valid nlattr header; reading `mask[0].nla_len` triggers MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.code: struct nlattr mask[1024 / sizeof(struct nlattr)]; struct ofpbuf maskbuf = OFPBUF_STUB_INITIALIZER(mask);
fine_trace.note: Allocates the stack array `mask` without initialization and wraps it in an empty stub ofpbuf. On entry to the helper, `maskbuf.base` and `maskbuf.data` both point at `mask`, while `maskbuf.size` is 0, so no nlattr header exists until parser code explicitly writes one.

Inside the `set(` action branch, parse_odp_action() passes the attacker-controlled payload after `set(` together with the empty stack-backed `maskbuf` into the generic key/mask parser. For the staged PoC, the helper input starts with `ufid:cb999996-9996-0996-0447-009000000009)`.

fine_trace.code: if (ovs_scan(s, "ufid:")) { s += 5; if (!uuid_from_string_prefix((struct uuid *)ufid, s)) { return -EINVAL; } s += UUID_LEN; return s - s_; }
fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled set payload begins with `ufid:` and the staged UUID is well formed, so odp_ufid_from_string() accepts it and returns a positive consumed length of 41 characters.

fine_trace.code: int ufid_len = odp_ufid_from_string(s, &ufid); if (ufid_len) { return ufid_len; }
fine_trace.note: Because `ufid_len > 0`, parse_odp_key_mask_attr() returns immediately before any later `SCAN_*` path appends a key attribute to `actions` or a mask attribute to `maskbuf`. The caller receives a success length but both buffers are still unchanged from entry.

In the staged PoC, the character immediately after the 41-byte UFID payload is `)`, so this syntactic check passes. No companion guard verifies that `maskbuf.size > 0` or that `actions` gained a child nlattr before control continues into the size calculations.

The local `mask` array is still the stack storage from step 1, and step 4 never wrote a Netlink header into it. parse_odp_action() nevertheless passes `mask` to nl_attr_get_size() as though `mask[0]` were a populated struct nlattr.

MSAN sink. nl_attr_get_size() reads `nla->nla_len` from the caller-supplied pointer, which aliases step 1's uninitialized `mask[0]`. The uninitialized header read is reported at `lib/netlink.c:598:5`, with the origin attributed to the `mask` stack allocation in parse_odp_action().

allocation_context.note: The MSAN trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `mask` in the stack frame of `parse_odp_action` at line 2162; the concrete stack array declaration used by this trace is at line 2215.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The poisoned bytes originate from the `mask` stack array in parse_odp_action(), while the logical bug is the UFID fast path in parse_odp_key_mask_attr() that returns success without populating that array.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix removes UFID parsing from parse_odp_key_mask_attr() and handles UFID only in odp_flow_from_string(), so a `set(ufid:...)` payload no longer reaches nl_attr_get_size(mask) with an empty stack-backed mask buffer.

poc.trigger: /bin/arvo run in the vulnerable ARVO image executes /out/odp_target on /tmp/poc and reproduces MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value in nl_attr_get_size.

format.name: NUL-terminated OVS datapath action string
format.contract: The staged PoC is the exact ASCII string `set(ufid:cb999996-9996-0996-0447-009000000009)\0`. It is accepted by the harness because it is NUL-terminated and newline-free. Its trigger semantics are that the entire `set(` payload is a valid `ufid:<uuid>` token followed immediately by `)`, so parse_odp_key_mask_attr() returns a positive length without appending any key or mask nlattrs before parse_odp_action() calls nl_attr_get_size(mask) on the still-uninitialized stack-backed mask buffer.
